claim: Real code execution, not model-simulated execution, carries most of the program-aided gain (PAL: 72.0 with interpreter vs 23.2 with model-simulated runtime vs 19.7 direct, GSM8K, Codex, 3-run average). [Gap search: ToRL and Chain of Code support real execution on AIME and BBH, but neither is an equal-token real-versus-simulated ablation.]
agent_test: At equal tokens compare: CoT, program written and run by a real interpreter, program written but result simulated by the model. One model, GSM8K plus a harder-numbers variant.

claim: An external executor keeps accuracy when numbers get large (GSM-HARD): PAL falls from 72.0 to about 61 while CoT falls from 65.6 to about 20-23. Exact cells differ between text and table of the same paper.
agent_test: Swap numbers in a held-out math set for larger ones; measure the drop for CoT vs code-plus-interpreter.

claim: Written intermediate work helps on multi-step computation the model cannot do in one pass (scratchpad: polynomial 8.8->20.1 few-shot, 31.8->50.7 fine-tuned; addition beyond training length fails without it), but did not help on real MBPP output prediction (5% vs 10%).
agent_test: Test with and without a visible scratch field on long-chain arithmetic and trace-execution items at equal tokens.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not help and often hurts: GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0 over two rounds; GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1. With an oracle label it helps (GPT-4 95.5 -> 97.5; HotpotQA 49 -> 59). [Gap search: 2024 survey and SCoRe agree; Self-Correction Bench (2025) finds reasoning-trained models show near-zero blind spot when shown an injected error, and a Wait cue cuts the blind spot 89.3% in non-reasoning models, so the claim holds for prompted self-feedback on non-reasoning models only.]
agent_test: Compare same-model self-review against review with a program check or a ground-truth test, at equal calls. Include a no-review arm.

claim: Multi-agent debate gains over a single model are mostly explained by more samples: original Du et al. gains (arithmetic 67.0 -> 81.8, GSM8K 77.0 -> 85.0) shrink or vanish against self-consistency at equal responses in later work. [Gap search: token-matched 2026 test (FRAMES, MuSiQue) again has single agent best: 0.418 vs debate 0.388 at 1000 tokens.]
agent_test: Equal-token arms: self-consistency N, debate N agents x rounds, single model. Report on one fixed set.

claim: Reflection or self-check can lower accuracy in some settings (Du: MMLU 63.9 -> 57.7; GSM8K 77.0 -> 75.0; Reflexion Leetcode-Hard 77.1 vs 80.1 for GPT-4).
agent_test: Add a no-check arm on every task; check only when a verifier exists.

claim: Voting over many samples yields gains that grow with task difficulty and shrink on easy tasks (More Agents: GSM8K +12 to +24, MATH +6 to +10, Chess +1 to +4).
agent_test: Sweep N at fixed total tokens on easy vs hard items.

claim: Multi-agent systems fail often and for organisational reasons: 41% to 86.7% failure across 7 systems; modes include step repetition 15.7%, not recognising completion 12.4%, reasoning-action mismatch 13.2%; verification-related modes total about 23.5% (6.2+8.2+9.1) of annotated failures.
agent_test: Log the same failure modes in our runs; count premature stops and missing verification.

claim: Cheap structural fixes help multi-agent software tasks: role clarification +9.4% and a high-level verification step +15.6% on ChatDev (one system, one model).
agent_test: Add an explicit final verification step to our loop; compare with and without at equal tokens.

claim: Architecture gains depend on task structure: on sequential planning every multi-agent variant lost 39% to 70%; on parallelisable finance centralized reached 0.631 vs single 0.349; where single agent is already above about 45% extra agents give negative returns; independent agents amplified errors 17.2x vs 4.4x centralized (but error amplification itself was not a significant regressor, beta 0.014, p=.658). [Gap search: Kim is token-matched but per-cell CI about 20 points at n=20; Tran and Kiela 2026 confirm single agent is the default on multi-hop QA.]
agent_test: Route: one thread on sequential tasks, decompose only when subtasks are independent. Test the 45% threshold on our own tasks.

claim: LLM-Modulo (model proposes, external verifiers critique, backprompt up to 15 times) lifts planning far above the autonomous model: 12% autonomous vs 82% Blocks World, 70% Logistics; numbers are quoted from other papers.
agent_test: Replicate a small Blocks World set with a rule-based verifier vs model self-critique at equal calls.

claim: External memory management for LLM context can improve retrieval: MemGPT deep-memory retrieval 32.1% -> 92.5% (GPT-4), 38.7% -> 66.9% (GPT-3.5); authors' own benchmark, LLM judge. [Gap search: MemoryAgentBench, an independent test, shows memory agents score below long-context models: MemGPT 28.3, Mem0 21.1 vs GPT-4o 48.8.]
agent_test: Test paging of notes vs full context at equal tokens on a long-conversation recall set.

claim: A persistent skill library and curriculum make an agent accumulate capability (Voyager: 63 unique items, 3.3x baselines; removing the skill library plateaus progress), but only in Minecraft with GPT-4 and 3 runs.
agent_test: Ablate stored reusable routines in our loop on repeated task families.

claim: Verbalised reasoning can be unfaithful: biasing features cut accuracy by up to 36% across 13 BBH tasks without the explanation mentioning the bias. Written reasoning is a weak trace of what the model used. [Gap search: Chen 2025 on reasoning models: faithfulness 25% (Claude 3.7) and 39% (R1).]
agent_test: Check whether our scratch notes mention an injected hint when answers shift.

claim: Heavy reliance on a language model for writing reduced later recall of own text (quote failure 15/18 vs 2/18 vs 2/18, N=54, p<.001) in a non-peer-reviewed preprint; a human result, not evidence about an agent.
agent_test: Not testable on an agent; keep as boundary on human-AI offloading claims.

claim: The Google-effect style priming claim (computer-word Stroop slowing) did not replicate: BF01 = 5.07 for the null on N=89 analysed of 117 tested (hard-question RT 825 vs 821 ms). This does not refute offloading in general.
agent_test: Not agent-relevant beyond cautioning against citing priming-based offloading evidence.

claim: Acting on the world to simplify thinking is common in humans: Tetris players rotate pieces more than needed to place them (expected 1.5 rotations; observed higher) at about 100 ms per physical rotation vs 800-1200 ms mentally. Subject count and exact means not extracted. [Gap search: Kirsh and Maglio 1994 re-read: mental-rotation pilot had 3 subjects; no independent replication found.]
agent_test: Give the agent a cheap external action (run a probe) and compare against pure thought at equal tokens.

claim: Physical interactivity helps when a mental load is imposed: with token-moving, the suppression cost shrank (N=52; 63.5 vs 44.6 percent with suppression, against 56.0 vs 26.9 in low interactivity). Insight problems solved more with interactivity (N=63, N=55). One lab team; digits of a22 not re-verified.
agent_test: Check numbers against the primary text before use; then test written workspace vs none.

claim: Cockpit speed bugs and checklists act as memory that no single crew member holds; qualitative, from over 100 observed flights, no error rates.
agent_test: Treat as design motivation only; not a measured effect.

claim: The theory supplies a framing, not a falsifiable prediction: founding papers are ethnographic or conceptual with no effect sizes, and the AI papers read do not cite Hutchins. Evidence for 'model + program + checks is one system' is by analogy and from engineering ablations.
agent_test: Frame benchmarks as component ablations (code, check, memory) rather than tests of the theory.

claim: Replication base rate for social-science experiments is moderate: 13/21 (62%) replicated, effect about half the original size.
agent_test: Use as a prior: discount single-lab effects (e.g. interactivity) by about half.

claim: At matched thinking tokens a single agent is the best default on multi-hop QA across four current model families: mean accuracy at 1000 tokens single 0.418 vs debate 0.388, roles 0.381, sequential 0.379, subtask-parallel 0.369, ensemble 0.333; multi-agent leads only at 100 tokens or under heavy context corruption.
agent_test: Run single chain vs voting vs debate at equal tokens on our own tasks; expect single to win unless context is degraded.

claim: The 45% single-agent threshold from Kim et al. is a fitted prior, not a law: it was derived on the same six benchmarks (94% match, per-cell CI about 20 points at n=20) and has not been tested outside them. Kim's design is already token-matched (mean 4,800 reasoning tokens).
agent_test: Measure our single-agent baseline per task type; use 45% only as a starting guess.

claim: Reasoning-model traces are only partly faithful: Claude 3.7 Sonnet 25% and DeepSeek R1 39% of hint-use cases are verbalised; RL reward hacks are verbalised under 2% in 5 of 6 environments. A trace is evidence, not an audit.
agent_test: Never accept a claim on the trace alone; require an executable check.

claim: Self-correction depends on who produced the error: 14 non-reasoning models have a 64.5% blind spot on their own errors but fix the same error placed in the user turn; reasoning-trained models show about zero blind spot (R1-Distill-70B -0.031 to -0.050) and a Wait cue cuts the blind spot 89.3%.
agent_test: Test re-entry cues (Wait, role flip) as a cheap layer before the external check.

claim: External memory designs are not a free gain in an independent benchmark: long-context GPT-5-mini scores 60.6 overall vs MemGPT 28.3, Mem0 21.1, BM25 RAG 41.5; RAG wins only on accurate retrieval (BM25 60.5 vs 49.2 backbone); selective forgetting stays at or below 28% except GPT-5-mini.
agent_test: Compare plain long context to a notes file to retrieval on our tasks, scoring retrieval and forgetting separately.

claim: Extending one chain has diminishing and then negative returns; parallel paths with a vote can beat it at the same budget (up to 20% higher accuracy reported), and the best compute split depends on difficulty (more than 4x efficiency over best-of-N).
agent_test: Sweep chain length and sample count at fixed tokens by difficulty tier.

claim: Real code execution adds accuracy on harder tasks than GSM8K: AIME24 Qwen2.5-Math-7B Instruct 10.0, TIR 26.7, ToRL 43.3; BBH Chain of Code 84 vs CoT 72 (davinci-003). Python alone fails on semantic tasks, so a hybrid is needed. No equal-token real-vs-simulated ablation on 2025 models was found.
agent_test: Ablate interpreter vs simulated execution at equal tokens on our code and math items.

claim: Human offloading costs internal memory: with a trusted external list, recall dropped (N=40, t(38)=7.22, d=2.28) and relational clustering dropped (d=1.04). Organise external notes by relation.
agent_test: Compare flat vs categorised notes on later retrieval.

claim: No paper was found that tests distributed-cognition or extended-mind predictions (coupling, offloading threshold) directly on LLM agents; searches this round were limited by API rate limits and a spent search budget, so the absence is weakly supported.
agent_test: Repeat the search when rate limits reset.
